:::{#thm-wrong-code}
#### The cost of coding with the wrong distribution

Let $X$ take finitely many values, with probability mass function $p$.
Suppose a code is built for a different probability mass function $q$,
with $q(x) > 0$ wherever $p(x) > 0$,
by giving each value the length $\ell(x) = \lceil -\log_2 q(x) \rceil$.
Then its expected length $L$ under $p$ satisfies

$$H_2(p, q) \le L < H_2(p, q) + 1,$$

where $H_2(p, q)$ is the
[cross-entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cross-entropy)
of $q$ relative to $p$, with base-2 logarithms.

:::

::: {.proof}

Rounding up adds less than one binary digit, so for every $x$

$$-\log_2 q(x) \le \ell(x) < -\log_2 q(x) + 1.$$

Multiply each part by $p(x) \ge 0$ and sum over the values of $X$.
Since $\sum_{x} p(x) = 1$,

$$
-\sum_{x} p(x) \log_2 q(x)
\le \sum_{x} p(x) \, \ell(x)
< -\sum_{x} p(x) \log_2 q(x) + 1.
$$

The middle sum is $L$, and the outer sums are $H_2(p, q)$.

:::
